extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: Common Corpus is the largest open dataset for language model pre-training, containing approximately two trillion tokens of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed text across six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Code, Open Web, and Open Semantic. It supports multilingual pre-training across major European and low-resource languages.
extraction.license: Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Open license, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.inLanguage: English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, Russian, and multiple other languages
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were assembled from collections in the public domain and under permissive open licenses through collections-as-data (CAD) dumps, web APIs, and direct extractions from specialized repositories across government, cultural heritage, scientific publishing, open-source code repositories, web sources, and semantic knowledge graphs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Web Scraping, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw sources include SEC EDGAR, WTO, AMF, TED EU Tenders, GATT Library, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, Eurovoc, French Open Data (DILA), USPTO, UN Digital Library, Chronicling America, Europeana, Gallica, Biblioteca Digital Hispánica, Delpher, OpenAlex, arXiv, The Stack v1 and v2, Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube Commons, StackExchange, and Wikidata.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) was replaced with fictitious but realistic values using Presidio and custom regular expressions. For documents identified with harmful language by the Celadon classifier, content was either removed or synthetically rewritten. Wikidata RDF triples were translated into natural language sequences without textual synthesis.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation was conducted using Segmentext. OCR error detection was performed using OCRoscope (evaluating non-recognized 7-grams via cld2) and OCRerrcr (DeBERTa-v2 model). OCR correction and restructuring were conducted using OCRonos (based on Llama 3 8B). Code files were filtered to remove unwanted extensions (e.g., svg, csv, json), non-permissible licenses, and files containing 75% or more digits, with newline sequence normalization. PII was detected and replaced via Presidio, and toxicity was filtered using the Celadon classifier.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: fastText, cld2, Segmentext, OCRoscope, OCRerrcr, OCRonos, Microsoft Presidio, Celadon
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Available on Hugging Face partitioned into 10,000 Parquet files. Conceived as an evolving open science infrastructure with Hugging Face providing archiving of past versions for reproducibility, and ongoing expansions planned for European and African languages via the LLMs4EU project.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses present in the source data was detected and replaced with fictitious values.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables pre-training of open, legally compliant, and auditable LLMs conforming to strict data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, EU AI legislation) without relying on fair use, mitigating copyright infringement risks and addressing the rapid restriction of the AI data commons.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Public domain cultural heritage content dating back 80+ years exhibits historical cultural norms, including racial, gender, sexual, religious, ability biases, and depictions of violence. The dataset is linguistically skewed towards major European languages, with Open Science being ~85% English, and low-resource/African languages having shallow representation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Subject to an open data paradox where large portions of open content remain uncollected; shallow coverage of low-resource languages; size (2 trillion tokens) is insufficient for frontier-scale models; lacks instruction-tuning or task-specific fine-tuning data; curation/filtering tools (OCR correction, PII masking, toxicity classification) do not guarantee 100% precision.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training Large Language Models (LLMs) and Small Language Models (SLMs), developing multimodal vision-language and speech models, pre-training retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models, feature visualization research, and creating secondary synthetic datasets or benchmarks.
